frontier.hypothesis: H_a0ptr_vfirst (2/83) already carries both of block 0's target operands; if the shift can be emitted two slots later - after the prologue sw $s0,0x10($sp) and the copy move $s0,$s2 - the function closes from the v1-first side without touching the crown at all.
frontier.mechanism: Both insns are INSN_PRIORITY 1 and class 3 against the prologue store, so rank_for_schedule falls through to sched.c:2461-2463's INSN_LUID compare and preserves source order; the trace taken this session (dumps_H/sched_debug.txt) confirms val=0 ties in block 0 on the new chassis. A priority of 2 requires a predecessor whose insn_cost is 2 (a load feeding the insn); a class below 3 requires a cost>1 LOG_LINKS relation to last_scheduled_insn.
frontier.next_probe: Read dumps_H/text1a_c.sched2 block 0 end-to-end and identify which insn ids are the copy and the shift on this chassis, then enumerate source shapes that give the COPY a load predecessor (its source arriving through a value block 0 already loads) or that delay the shift's readiness by giving it an in-block consumer later than the guard's slt. Measure any candidate that keeps build_insns at 83.

frontier.hypothesis: On the i-first chassis, a real write to the parameter pseudo (reg 72) placed between the block-0 shift and the loop-1 guard flips qty_first_reg back to i, which would give that chassis both operands at once.
frontier.mechanism: cse's invalidate() calls delete_reg_equiv(), which promotes reg_next_eqv to qty_first_reg when the current canonical register is written; every use after that point is canonicalised to i while the shift, already processed, keeps reg 72. The self-assignment spelling is folded by expand (s53) and the dead-store spelling is deleted by jump.c:577 (s51), so what is needed is a write the function performs anyway.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate values block 0 must compute that could legally land in the parameter (the D_800A33AC reload, the D_800EED14 element address, s4 + a1) while still leaving the original a0 value available to loop 2's preheader copy - e.g. by having the preheader read a second preserved copy that the target's move $s0,$s2 could itself be. Measure each with sandbox and reject anything at build_insns != 83.

frontier.hypothesis: Form A's loop-2 callee-save rotation (build offset=$s0 / counter=$s1 against target offset=$s1 / counter=$s0) is an independent defect; undoing it while keeping the offset-reuse crown defeat should drop form A's score from 11 toward a block-0-only residual.
frontier.mechanism: Both loop-2 pseudos are callee-save because they cross the indirect call; which one gets $s0 follows global.c's allocno_compare priority (floor_log2(n_refs)*n_refs/live_length), and form A's offset pseudo inherits the block-0 copy's longer live range so it outranks the counter. The target gives the offset $s1 - the register sum occupies until func_800520B8.
frontier.next_probe: Vary the reference counts and live ranges of form A's two loop-2 pseudos (offset initialised from v1 vs from the pointer, exit test hoisted or not, offset uses split across the D_800EED1C and D_800EED10 loads), read tmp/grind/func_80045294/dumps/text1a_c.greg for the allocation order after each change, and measure only shapes that stay at 83 instructions.
